WEC Energy Group.why: Wisconsin regulated utility building gas, renewable and battery generation and transmission to serve Very Large Customer data centers (Microsoft's I-94 corridor campus south of Milwaukee; the Vantage Data Centers / Oracle Port Washington site); a growing share of its rate base is dedicated to these data-center loads.
WEC Energy Group.evidence: WEC Energy Group Q2 FY2026 (07-29-2026), CEO Scott Lauber: 'Construction continues at the Microsoft site in Pleasant Prairie, and the first data center facility is fully operational... We are preparing to serve a forecasted demand increase of 2.6 GW in this region through 2030'

players.product: Regulated electric service under the Very Large Customer (VLC) tariff, with new gas, renewable and battery generation and transmission built for Microsoft's data center campus in the I-94 corridor south of Milwaukee and the Vantage Data Centers / Oracle site at Port Washington, Wisconsin

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 earnings of $0.91 a share, a $0.15 increase versus Q2 2025; rate base growth contributed $0.13, including $0.09 of incremental AFUDC equity and $0.02 of cash returns on projects under construction, mostly projects supporting the VLC customers. Weather-normal retail electric sales grew 4.2%, driven by growth from the VLCs; excluding the iron ore mine and the VLC customers, sales grew 1.2%.
quarterly_data.figure: EPS $0.91 (+$0.15 YoY); weather-normal retail electric sales +4.2%

quarterly_data.signal: Reaffirmed 2026 earnings guidance of $5.51-$5.61 a share (normal weather assumed); Q3 2026 guidance $0.92-$0.98 a share. Long-term EPS growth of 7%-8% a year (compound) between 2026 and 2030, which management expects to accelerate to the upper half of the range starting in 2028; full year 2026 weather-normalized electric sales excluding the iron ore mine and VLC customers expected to be relatively even with 2025.

Five-year capital plan of $37.5 billion of projected investments, a good portion serving the very large customers; by the end of 2030 approximately 15% of the asset base is expected to be dedicated to these very large customers. An updated capital plan will be shared on the Q3 call; CEO named growth at the current data center sites (the I-94 corridor), a potential additional large customer, transmission growth and possible Point Beach replacement generation as upside, much of it in the 2030-2031 timeframe 'because... it really takes that long from a supply chain'.
quarterly_data.figure: $37.5 billion five-year capital plan; ~15% of asset base for very large customers by end of 2030

quarterly_data.signal: Vantage Data Centers is developing facilities for Oracle on approximately 1,900 acres north of Milwaukee (Port Washington); the initial phase is being built on 670 acres, Vantage has stated it expects to invest $15 billion to complete this phase in 2028, and the first facility could come online as soon as late 2027. WEC has 1.3 GW of demand for the Vantage site in its five-year forecast, and the site has the potential to reach 3.5 GW over time. Oracle is currently under payment cancellation agreements with credit support and enters the VLC service agreements on June 1st of next year; CEO: construction is 'on time, it's on budget', and the Oracle court case over the tariff's credit requirement is not expected to affect this project.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.3 GW in five-year forecast; potential 3.5 GW; $15 billion Vantage phase investment

quarterly_data.signal: Construction continues on new natural gas generation facilities in Paris and Oak Creek, Wisconsin, expected to start coming online in late 2027. CEO: Oracle and Microsoft have signed up for an 'all of the above' approach with renewables, batteries and natural gas; the next five-year plan may include a combined cycle rather than only simple cycle. Point Beach nuclear PPA: the first 500 MW comes due in December 2030 and the next 500 MW in March 2033; rule of thumb about a gigawatt is about $2 billion-$2.5 billion; a generation plan will be finalized on the Q3 call.
quarterly_data.figure: Paris and Oak Creek gas plants online from late 2027; Point Beach 500 MW (Dec 2030) + 500 MW (Mar 2033)

quarterly_data.signal: New data center prospects: CEO says WEC continues to have 'really good discussions with potential new, very large customers', probably not as large as the first two, 'more in that 400 to 500 MW size'; he cautioned not to expect 'three or four that are going to come in any day now' and does not expect collateral requirements to hurt new customer talks.
quarterly_data.figure: prospective VLCs of 400 to 500 MW each

quarterly_data.signal: Very Large Customer tariff: the Wisconsin PSC provided the written order in May; VLCs pay their full share of the cost. The tariff stands with a credit requirement of an A-; customers rated BBB- or worse must post collateral, which ramps with WEC's spending up to the assets' net book value, and customers sign up for 20 years for wind and solar. CEO: all three rating agencies viewed the filing favorably.
quarterly_data.figure: A- credit requirement; collateral at BBB- or worse; 20-year terms for wind and solar

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on data center pushback in Wisconsin: one gubernatorial candidate has identified a potential data center moratorium and several communities have raised moratoriums; WEC's rate case shows about $100 million of savings for customers over the next two years from the value of the data centers, and its generation water consumption is projected to be down about 25%-30% from 2015 to 2030.
quarterly_data.figure: about $100 million customer savings over two years; generation water use down 25%-30%

quarterly_data.signal: Labor constraint: WEC reduced 2026 spending on the Peoples Gas PIPE retirement program in Chicago because getting a labor force has been more challenging amid economic development 'from data centers to generation'; CEO expects to ramp the workforce up in 2027.

Regulatory: Wisconsin rate request for forward test years 2027 and 2028 filed in April, final orders expected by year-end with new rates effective January 2027 and 2028; the Illinois Commerce Commission approved the Rider QIP and bad debt rider settlements resolving 12 open dockets, and an Illinois decision for test year 2027 is expected by year-end. CEO: WEC is working with DOE on potential loans for gas generation; new nuclear at the Kewaunee site is a longer-term option only.

connects_to.relationship: Electric service and new generation for Microsoft's data center campus in the I-94 corridor south of Milwaukee (Very Large Customer tariff)

contracts.signal: Construction continues at the Microsoft site in Pleasant Prairie and the first data center facility is fully operational; Microsoft has purchased more than 2,200 acres in the I-94 corridor south of Milwaukee. WEC is preparing to serve a forecasted demand increase of 2.6 GW in this region through 2030, with opportunity for further expansion; CEO: substations are moving ahead of schedule and he anticipates 'something a little bit more' in MW at the Q3 plan update.
contracts.units: 2.6 GW forecasted regional demand increase through 2030; more than 2,200 acres
